definition: A device is at a customer while its asset status is RENTED: it carries that customer on the asset and has one running rental contract.

basis.customers: organisations that are neither a supplier nor a manufacturer, whether or not they hold a device now; one row each
basis.since: start of the customer's first rental contract; the model stores no onboarding date for a customer
basis.devices_at_customer: assets with status RENTED, by the customer on the asset
basis.contracts_ending_90d: running contracts whose planned end is between today and today + 90 days; the total is the sum over the customers' rows
basis.returns_overdue: running contracts whose planned end has passed: the device is still out after its contract ended; the total is the sum over the customers' rows
basis.returns_by_month: a customer's running contracts by the month of their planned end, from today; overdue ones are not repeated
basis.returns_schedule: every running contract, whichever organisation holds it, by the month of its planned end, from today; overdue ones are in returns_overdue_total
basis.returns_overdue_total: every running contract whose planned end has passed, whichever organisation holds it
basis.returns_after_window: every running contract whose planned end is after the last month of the grid
basis.rented_total: every asset with status RENTED, whether or not its customer is one of the rows
basis.customers_holding_devices: customers with at least one asset with status RENTED
basis.inbound_open_pos: outstanding units (ordered minus received) of open purchase order lines (PENDING, APPROVED, PLACED, PARTIALLY_RECEIVED), by the month of the line's estimated delivery date
basis.inbound_open_pos_late: the same lines whose estimated delivery date is before as_of
basis.inbound_open_pos_no_eta: the same lines without an estimated delivery date
basis.inbound_open_pos_after_window: the same lines whose estimated delivery date is after the last month of the grid
basis.inbound_open_total: every outstanding unit on the open lines: the months, late, no date and after the grid together
basis.defects: reported: rentals ended for a defect or a swap, by the end date; in_repair: devices in repair now, by the day they entered repair; repairs_invoiced: repair partner invoices, by the invoice date; written_off: devices recycled, the exit without proceeds, by the exit date. The last month is the current one, up to as_of. Reported: in the seeded data (app.seed_daas) a rental ends for a defect only for the devices that are in repair on the seed day, and those rentals ended in the weeks before it; the seed writes no defect history before that, and the demo simulation ends rentals as planned or early only, so every other month reads 0. Those zeros are a property of the simulated data, not of the business. Repairs invoiced: in the seeded data (app.seed_daas) a repair invoice exists only for a grade C device that went on to a second rental, dated at least eight days before that rental began, and the devices in repair on the seed day carry none yet; so a current month that began less than eight days before the seed day reads 0 until the simulation's repair-done event writes new invoices. Those zeros are a property of the simulated data, not of the business
basis.in_repair_now: every asset with status REPAIR, whatever sent it there (a defect or a grade C return): not a count of defects. defects[].in_repair spreads it over the months the devices entered repair; in_repair_before_window and in_repair_undated hold the rest
basis.in_repair_before_window: devices in repair now that entered repair before the first month of the defects grid
basis.in_repair_undated: devices in repair now without the date they entered it: in the total, in no month

omissions: defects[].replacements_consumed: no row links a defect return to the replacement device, and the movement log (asset_event) that would show swap-buffer devices going out holds no seeded history, so seeded months would read as false zeros

defects[].reported, the history: in the seeded data (app.seed_daas) a rental ends for a defect only for the devices that are in repair on the seed day, and those rentals ended in the weeks before it; the seed writes no defect history before that, and the demo simulation ends rentals as planned or early only, so every other month reads 0.
